claims.text: Cabinda is an exclave and province of Angola, a status that has been disputed by several political organisations in the territory.
Cabinda has an area of 7,290 km2 and a population of 903,370 at the 2024 census.
Portugal first claimed sovereignty over Cabinda in the February 1885 Treaty of Simulambuco, which gave it the status of a protectorate.
Cabinda is separated from the rest of Angola by a narrow strip of territory belonging to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Adjacent to the coast are some of the largest offshore oil fields in the world; Cabinda produces 700,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
